title: SLO orchestration crossfunctional mesh plan
content:
Context:
We are working toward an operational model that lets feature teams declare SLOs as first-class contracts and have a lightweight orchestration layer (the "mesh") enforce, observe, and automate runbook actions across Dedicated/Hosted/Private deployments. This doc lays out a cross-functional project plan to prototype a minimal SLO orchestration mesh, validate it with 2 pilot services, and hand off a repeatable playbook for scaling across product teams.

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
- Prototype a policy-as-code SLO contract format (YAML) that teams can check into repo and register with the control plane.
- Build an orchestration mesh that: accepts contracts, wires telemetry->SLO evaluation, and triggers automated remediation playbooks (notifications, autoscale hints, model-fallbacks).
- Validate with two pilot services (chat-generation, embeddings-indexer) and measure SLO compliance, noise (false alerts), and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for remediations.
- Produce a reproducible onboarding playbook + templates so feature teams can adopt with <2 days effort.

Proposed mesh architecture (prototype scope):
- Control plane (platform): policy registry, contract validator, rollout manager.
- Evaluation plane (lightweight): SLO evaluator service that consumes traces/metrics and emits signals (OK/WARN/VIOLATION).
- Actuation adapters: Slack pager, Ops webhook (PagerDuty), autoscale suggestion service, model-variant fallback controller.
- Lightweight sidecar/agent (optional for Private): small shim that sends required metrics and accepts actuation commands.
- Observability integration: use existing tracing + metrics export; add named SLO metrics (slo_window_count, slo_window_violations).

Roles & stakeholders:
- Platform eng (owner): Marisol Rivera — control plane & onboarding flow
- Observability (partner): Ethan Park — SLO metric definitions, alert tuning
- Serving runtime / Model infra: Priya Nair — model-fallback adapter & performance knobs
- SRE / Oncall: Zoe Kim — runbook authoring, incident response criteria
- Product pilot leads: Liam O'Connor (chat), TBD (embeddings) — validate UX and acceptance

Minimum viable deliverables (MVP):
- SLO contract spec (YAML) + validator CLI
- SLO evaluator microservice with a mocked telemetry adapter for local testing
- Two actuation adapters (Slack + autoscale-suggestion webhook)
- Pilot onboarding guide (step-by-step) and template repo (example contracts for chat & embeddings)
- Acceptance tests and basic dashboards (per-pilot SLO dashboard)

8-week sprint plan (high level):
- Week 0 (prework): confirm telemetry gaps, pick pilot teams, align KTs
- Week 1: contract spec draft + validator prototype; initial control-plane API design
- Week 2: evaluator service basic loop + ingestion stub; define success metrics
- Week 3: build Slack and webhook adapters; initial runbook templates
- Week 4: onboard pilot A (chat) to the mesh in shadow mode (no actuations)
- Week 5: iterate on alert thresholds, reduce noise; pilot A runbook automation enabled (limited scope)
- Week 6: onboard pilot B (embeddings) in shadow; integration testing across failure modes
- Week 7: enable actuations for pilot B; run a planned degradation exercise (chaos) and measure MTTM
- Week 8: retrospective, finalize onboarding playbook, handoff materials to SRE enablement and feature teams

Key metrics / acceptance criteria:
- False alert rate <= 15% after tuning for pilot services
- Median MTTM for automated remediations < 4 minutes (for covered remediations)
- Successful end-to-end onboarding for a pilot team in <= 2 days (documented steps)
- SLO contract validator blocks invalid contracts and provides actionable linting messages

Dependencies (hard + soft):
- Telemetry completeness: request/response latency histograms, error counters, trace sampling aligned with SLO windows (hard)
- PD/oncall routing agreement for automated actuations (soft/human policy)
- Feature-team sprint bandwidth to install agents or register contracts (soft)
- Private deployment shim (for enterprise customers) — may be out-of-scope for MVP but must be designed for

Runbooks & automation:
- Provide a 3-tier runbook model: observe -> assess -> act. Each SLO contract must reference a runbook id.
- Automations allowed for low-risk remediations (scale-up hint, reduce batch size, model fallback). All high-impact actions require a confirm workflow.
- Capture a template runbook that maps a violation signal to playbook steps and recovery verification checks.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy SLO definitions causing alert fatigue. Mitigation: shadow mode for 2 weeks + automatic suppression windows.
- Risk: telemetry gaps prevent accurate evaluation. Mitigation: instrumentation sprint and a gating checklist before onboard.
- Risk: actuation causing customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: start with advisory actuations, require human-confirm for any change to model runtime.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we support composite SLOs (multi-signal e.g., latency + quality) in MVP or postpone? (proposal: basic support via boolean expressions, full feature later)
- What is the allowed blast radius for automated actuations? (policy to be defined by Security & SRE)
- How will SLO ownership be represented in org metadata? tagging vs. repo-level ownership?

Communication cadence & channels:
- Weekly sync (30m) — platform / observability / SRE / two pilot leads (calendar invite: "SLO Mesh Standup")
- Slack channel: #slo-mesh-proto (platform-owned) — use for async status and blockers
- Retrospective at end of pilot with a decision log and next steps

Immediate actions (next 7 days):
- Marisol: publish contract spec strawman and open PR against template repo
- Ethan: run telemetry gap analysis for chat + embeddings and publish checklist
- Priya: prototype model-fallback adapter API surface and share latency/cost tradeoffs
- Zoe: draft minimal runbook template and incident acceptance criteria

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Consider a "slo-shadow-mode" flag at registration time so teams can see predictions before enforcement.
- Iterate contract linter with examples where SLO window is too small for noisy signals.
- Pilot must include an explicit user-impact scenario (e.g., slow tokens on chat) so we can exercise fallback.

References & links:
- existing reliability playbooks (link to CONFLUENCE-7890)
short_description: Draft cross-functional plan to build a minimal SLO orchestration mesh: spec, evaluator, adapters, pilots, and onboarding playbook.
